messages.author: 7a756e4421f1bf6c
messages.subject: Fitting a configural model
parts:
Hi there
I need help, I'm doing measurement invariance in Lavaan using the following codes
CFA1 <- '
Physical Abuse =~ ICAST_PA_Kick + ICAST_PA_Obj + ICAST_PA_Hit
Emotional Abuse =~ ICAST_EA_Sho + ICAST_EA_Emb + ICAST_EA_Thrab + ICAST_EA_TES + ICAST_EA_Swo + ICAST_EA_Bordea
Sexual Abuse =~ ICAST_SA_Ups + ICAST_SA_Vid + ICAST_SA_Loo + ICAST_SA_Tou + ICAST_SA_Svid + ICAST_SA_Rap + ICAST_SA_Trap
Neglect =~ ICAST_CN_Eat + ICAST_CN_Sic + ICAST_CN_Car + ICAST_CN_Unimp + ICAST_CN_Sup
'
Model1 <- cfa(CFA1, data = Second, meanstructure = T, estimator = 'WLSMV')

to fit the configural model, I'm using the following code
Configural1 <- cfa(model = Model1,
                   data = Second,
                   meanstructure = TRUE,
                   mimic = "Mplus",
                   estimator = "WLSMV",
                   missing = "listwise",
                   group = "Country")

However, I'm getting the following error;

Warning messages:
1: In lavaan::lavaan(model = Model1, data = Second, group = "Country",  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Model estimation FAILED! Returning starting values.
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = Model1, data = Second, group = "Country",  :
  lavaan WARNING: estimation of the baseline model failed.


Any help will be highly appreciated

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Fitting a configural model
parts:
You haven't declared any variables as ordered=.  Are they already of that class in the data.frame?

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

It is not easy to guess with so little information, but you could try fitting each 1-factor model separately, to try narrowing down when the problem occurs.
